rows.definition: The typed omission fitplan reports (value context_unknown) when the model header carries no context_length, so neither Plan nor the T04 joint search can bound the requested context from facts.
rows.distinction: An input-gap marker, not a refusal: the pool may still fit and the serve boot proceeds fail-open on today's sizing; unlike ReasonContextExceedsPool nothing was priced and found too big.

rows.definition: The typed omission fitplan reports (value host_pool_capacity_unknown) when a discrete topology's host DRAM pool size cannot be probed, so host-scoped weight and ring rows are priced without a host-side cap.
rows.distinction: A probe-gap marker on the HOST pool of a discrete topology only; OmitPoolCapacityUnknown covers the device pool, and neither is a refusal - the plan continues on whatever capacity was readable.

rows.definition: The typed omission fitplan reports (value pool_capacity_unknown) when the usable pool budget for the selected arm cannot be determined, so candidate rows are priced with an unknown pool term.
rows.distinction: A probe-gap marker on the DEVICE pool budget; OmitHostPoolCapacityUnknown names the same gap on a discrete topology's host pool, and neither refuses - pricing proceeds with the missing term flagged.

rows.definition: The typed refusal reason fitplan returns (value weights_exceed_pool) when the selected arm's weights alone exceed the usable pool before any KV or slot term is added, so no candidate row can fit.
rows.distinction: A weights-only infeasibility verdict: it stops a live --fit auto boot with exit 2 and names the shortfall bytes, whereas context/concurrency refusals mean the weights fit but the requested context or slots do not.

rows.definition: The Refusal.HostPool bool flag (JSON host_pool) marking that a weights_exceed_pool refusal is short on a discrete topology's host DRAM pool rather than the device pool.
rows.distinction: A side-of-the-topology marker on one refusal, not a pool descriptor: PoolUsableBytes and HostPoolUsableBytes carry the actual budgets, while this flag only says which pool the shortfall belongs to.

rows.definition: The unexported constructor that binds a fitplan Input (hardware, weights, demand, calibration) to the internal planner struct shared by Plan's single-arm pricing and the T04 joint context x KV-dtype x slots search.
rows.distinction: Builds the pricer; it does no ranking itself: Plan prices one preselected demand list while Search drives the same planner over a candidate grid and applies operator pins.

rows.definition: The cmd/fak glue that extracts the GGUF architecture string into the fitplan report so the --plan-json sizing artifact records which architecture the sizing ran under.
rows.distinction: A report-label extractor, not a planner: it reads the loaded header for provenance display and feeds no sizing decision back into internal/fitplan.

rows.definition: The cmd/fak glue that snapshots the host hardware facts (backend, sizing-fit and host-fit budgets) into the fitplan Hardware block of the serve sizing artifact.
rows.distinction: Collects hardware evidence for the report only: the snapshot never mutates the pool budget, and all pricing happens inside internal/fitplan against that snapshot.

rows.definition: The serve resolver that picks which load arm (Q4K checkpoint vs full-precision) the native context budget sizes against, honoring the FAK_Q4K operator pin and the backend's offload posture.
rows.distinction: Chooses the ARM being sized, not the budget itself: resolveServeNativeContextBudget computes the token count for an already-chosen arm, while this decides which arm the operator pinned.
